answer: Run every identity through CedarBench, a 60-second timing fingerprint: eight CPU, memory, and network timings, median of three runs, pinned on-ledger. A new fingerprint must sit at least 20% away from every other identity's fingerprint, so clones sharing one machine form one island and are rejected as a group. Each epoch the fingerprint must mirror the identity's first fingerprint within 10%, or its weight freezes and 30 POA slashes. An honest operator pays for one machine, while a farm must pay for ten, so cost rises per fake while the chain checks distances from fingerprints.
